title: Kriti Sanon Just Crashed Bollywood's Most Exclusive Club. The Data Proves She Belongs.
excerpt: Ormax's 'Stars India Loves' ranking puts her alongside Alia, Deepika, Shraddha, and Katrina — the first new name in the Top 5 in six years. And she did it by surviving flops that would have ended anyone else.
body:
There is a list that every Bollywood actress knows exists, even if she pretends she doesn't. It's unwritten, unofficial, and brutally honest. It's the answer to: *who are the Top 5?*

For the better part of a decade, the answer barely changed. **Deepika Padukone**. **Alia Bhatt**. **Katrina Kaif**. **Kareena Kapoor Khan**. **Shraddha Kapoor**. A fortress. Occasionally, someone would knock on the door — a breakout role, a viral moment, a ₹100 crore hit — but the names at the top stayed the same, year after year, like they were carved into marble.

Until now.

According to Ormax Media's latest *Stars India Loves* data — arguably the most credible audience-sentiment tracker in Indian cinema — **Kriti Sanon** has broken into the Top 5 female Hindi film stars for 2025. She replaces **Kareena Kapoor Khan**, who had held her position since 2019. The rest of the list remains unchanged: Deepika, Alia, Katrina, and Shraddha are all still there. Four of the same five names from six years ago. Only one seat opened up, and Kriti took it.

This is not a pity promotion. This is not a studio-manufactured narrative. The Ormax rankings are based on audience engagement and perception data, not box office alone. And what makes Kriti's rise genuinely remarkable is not just that she made the list — it's the wreckage she walked through to get there.

## The Flop Years That Didn't Break Her

Rewind to 2022 and 2023. Kriti Sanon was in five films: ***Bachchhan Paandey***, ***Shehzada***, ***Adipurush***, ***Ganapath***, and ***Bhediya***. Between them, they represent a masterclass in how to pick the wrong project. *Adipurush* became a punchline. *Ganapath* opened to empty theaters. *Shehzada* was dead on arrival. These are the kinds of runs that end careers — quietly, without ceremony, the phone just stops ringing.

But something strange happened. Kriti's popularity *didn't dip*. The films failed. She didn't. Audiences — and, critically, the industry — could tell the difference. As Bollywood Hungama's analysis noted: "It was evident to everyone, from the industry to trade to the audiences, that it was the films and not Kriti which were failing."

That distinction is rare and precious. Bollywood is littered with actresses who were blamed for their films' failures even when the writing, direction, and male leads were the real problems. Kriti Sanon survived the blame game.

## The Comeback That Changed the Math

2024 flipped the script. ***Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya*** paired her with Shahid Kapoor and landed as a genuine hit — her performance as a robot was subtle, funny, and commercially potent. ***Crew***, with Tabu and Kareena, was a runaway success that proved she could hold her own in an ensemble of heavyweights. Her Netflix film ***Do Patti*** added streaming credibility. And in 2025, ***Tere Ishk Mein*** crossed the ₹100 crore mark, making her a certified solo box office draw.

That progression — from National Award winner (*Mimi*, 2021) to flop survivor (2022-23) to box office anchor (2024-25) — is the kind of trajectory that turns an actress into a *star*. Not someone who gets cast because she photographs well. Someone producers build films around.

## The Cocktail 2 Test

Which brings us to next week. **Cocktail 2** releases on June 19, and it might be the biggest test of Kriti's new status. The film pairs her with **Shahid Kapoor** (again) and **Rashmika Mandanna** in what's being positioned as the summer's sexiest romantic drama. Directed by **Homi Adajania**, backed by **Maddock Films** and **Luv Films**, with music by **Pritam** — the pedigree is immaculate.

The original *Cocktail* (2012) made **Deepika Padukone** a superstar. It was the film where audiences stopped seeing her as just a pretty face and started seeing her as a force. If *Cocktail 2* does the same for Kriti — or even comes close — the Ormax ranking won't just be validated. It'll look like an understatement.

The film is already the #1 most anticipated Indian movie on IMDb, with a 21% page view share. Its songs are everywhere. The trailer broke YouTube. If this lands, Kriti Sanon won't just be in the Top 5 — she'll be chasing the top.

## What the Numbers Really Say

Ormax's report reveals a broader truth about Bollywood's gender dynamics. The average age of the Top 5 male Hindi film stars has risen from 47 in 2019 to 54 in 2025. The women's list averages 37, up from 33, but the churn is healthier. Younger names like **Kiara Advani**, **Rashmika Mandanna**, and **Aneet Padda** are rising. The women's side of Bollywood is evolving. The men's side is calcifying.

For the diaspora, Kriti's rise matters because she represents the kind of star NRIs actually watch. She's in the streaming films. She's in the popcorn entertainers. She's in the festival darlings. She spans every mode of consumption that a viewer in Chicago or Birmingham or Brampton uses to stay connected to Hindi cinema.

So here's to the new member of the club. She didn't inherit the seat. She didn't lobby for it. She survived *Adipurush*, dusted herself off, and earned it the hard way.

The marble has a new name.
